incident-bot: [PAGE] p99 latency alert - hosted-us-west-2 pool · service=inference-hosted · alert_id=INC-2099994242

incident-bot: metrics snapshot: p95=210ms p99=2.9s streaming-stalls=0.9% · spike began ~20:05 UTC · route=/v1/generate (streaming)

Eli_oncall: I'm on call. Pulling traces and node health. @Raj_infra can you join? This looks like tail latency from infra side (possible hardware).

Raj_infra: joining now. Quick grep: accel-usw2-gpu-11 showing rising ECC corrected errors and occasional GPU resets in dmesg. accel-eu3-gpu-02 has recurring thermal throttle warnings.

Maya_ml: CS inbound — two customers filing truncated streams and slow interactive sessions. Tickets CS-4620, CS-4623. They see stalls of ~10-30s for some requests.

Eli_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) take affected nodes out of live rotation 2) route traffic to fallback quantized variant 3) increase client-side retry windows for streaming 4) start hardware probe and driver restart. I'll coordinate.

Raj_infra: cordoning accel-usw2-gpu-11 and accel-eu3-gpu-02. Running live drain:
```
kubectl cordon node/accel-usw2-gpu-11
kubectl drain node/accel-usw2-gpu-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Estimated traffic shift: ~400 qps.

ops-bot: routing: +400 qps -> fallback-model-v2-quant (p95 ~ 290ms). No error spike observed on fallback.

Eli_oncall: rolling restart of nvidia driver on accel-usw2-gpu-11. If restart doesn't clear ECC flooding, we'll RMA card. Also create an automatic fence rule: mark node unhealthy after 5 ECC corrections in 2m.

Raj_infra: driver restart in progress. Observed kernel log: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79" repeated; indicates possible GPU hardware fault. Temperature on accel-usw2-gpu-11 peaked at 91C under load earlier.

Maya_ml: customers updated with interim note: "We're re-routing your requests to a fallback variant to restore streaming reliability. Engineering is investigating root cause; we'll follow up with a timeline." They accepted short SLA credit proactively.

Sara_support: CS-4620 confirmed partial recovery after routing change; customer still saw a truncated stream and had to reconnect once. Logged clip and timestamp.

Eli_oncall: current numbers: p95=240ms p99=580ms streaming-stalls=0.2%. Improvement but we'll keep nodes cordoned. Created tracking ticket ENG-INC-THROTTLE-2099.

PM_Ryan: heads-up: if this repeats we'll need a status page update and possible customer outreach. Keep me in loop re: ETA for hardware swap and RCA.

Raj_infra: tentative root cause: one or more GPUs experiencing transient ECC correction floods triggering soft-resets; combined with elevated die temps -> throttling -> long tail latency for streaming stateful calls. Action items: schedule RMA for accel-usw2-gpu-11, apply driver/hotfix that reduces noisy recovery path, and tighten the probe to fence earlier.

Eli_oncall: next steps for post-incident: - leave nodes cordoned until RMA - implement fence rule (5 ECC corrections -> pool drain) - run 20m canary on fallback-model-v2-quant - add log sampling for streaming stalls to capture truncated payloads - draft postmortem and timeline.

incident-bot: incident state: mitigation applied · severity reduced to SEV-2 · page closed 20:50 UTC for active infra remediation. Please update ENG-INC-THROTTLE-2099 with notes.

Raj_infra: opened datacenter request DC-RMA-7891 for card swap; ETA 24-72h depending on parts. Also filing kernel-driver upgrade PR to staging to address noisy ECC path.

Maya_ml: collecting traces and examples of truncated streams to attach to customer follow-ups. Scheduling a customer check-in tomorrow morning.

Eli_oncall: handing off monitoring to night oncall (@Sara_support). If p99 > 1.5s or streaming-stalls > 0.5% re-pager @oncall-team. Leaving runbook and commands in ENG-INC-THROTTLE-2099.

Sara_support: on it. Dashboards open, alert thresholds lowered for the impacted pool for next 8h. Will escalate immediately if regression.

ops-bot: temporary monitor change: streaming-stalls threshold = 0.25% for pool hosted-us-west-2 for 8h.

Eli_oncall: thanks team. Filing this for postmortem review. :heart:
